narr: Thunderstorms developed along a dryline the evening of May 1 as an upper level disturbance swept across the forecast area. Some storms became severe as they moved across mainly Central Texas Wednesday night into Thursday morning. Additional storms developed Thursday night into Friday as a cold front moved through the area. Heavy rain causing flooding in Central Texas were the main impacts during this time period.
ev: A train derailment of 5 sand hauler cars occurred due to high water near CR 456 and CR 406.
TxDOT reported a road closure on Laney Street 2 miles north of Buffalo due to flooding of Buffalo Creek from heavy rainfall Wednesday night into Thursday morning.
Emergency management reported a washed out culvert/road on Dowell Road near Big Elm Creek 3 miles SSE of Moody due to heavy rainfall and flooding Thursday morning.
Emergency management reported several washed out roads/culverts across Central McLennan County due to heavy rainfall and flooding Thursday morning.
Emergency management reported multiple roads flooded in Mexia with one water rescue at 800 East Commerce Street.
Emergency management reported at least 16 roads closed with some wash-outs. Five road closures isolated residents.
Emergency management reported a portion of Bullhide Creek Rd in McClennan County was washed out due to heavy rainfall and flooding Thursday morning.

Multiple bridges along US 84 were reported with high water, including US 84 and the Lake Mexia Bridge. Multiple areas of flooding were also reported in Mexia including a stranded motorist at HWYs 14 and 171 in Mexia.
